item.research_question: How do Al and C additions affect the deformation mechanisms (dislocation slip vs. twinning) and strengthening contributions during cold rolling of a CoCrFeNiMn-type high-entropy alloy compared to the equiatomic reference?
item.material_system: CoCrFeNiMn-type HEA with composition (20–23) Co, Cr, Fe, Ni; 8.82 Mn; 3.37 Al; 0.69 C (at %)
item.processing_route: Self-propagating high-temperature synthesis (SHS) in a centrifugal setup followed by induction remelting in vacuum; cold rolling unidirectionally at room temperature with reductions of 5–10% per pass to final strains of 5%, 10%, 20%, 40%, 60%, and 80%
item.test_conditions: Room temperature tensile testing at an initial strain rate of 10⁻³ s⁻¹; microhardness testing with 0.3 kg load; microstructural analysis via XRD, EBSD, and TEM
key_findings: Initial as-cast alloy had a coarse-grained single fcc structure with grain size of 250–400 μm and yield strength of 210 MPa.
Uniform elongation of the as-cast alloy was 74%, decreasing to 1.3% after 80% cold rolling.
Yield strength increased from 210 MPa (as-cast) to 1310 MPa after 80% rolling reduction.
Dislocation density rose from ~1 × 10¹¹ m⁻² in the as-cast condition to ~2 × 10¹⁵ m⁻² after 40% strain.
Deformation twinning onset was delayed until 20% rolling reduction, whereas the equiatomic reference showed twins after 5%.
Substructure strengthening dominated at rolling reductions <40%, while grain (twin) boundary strengthening prevailed at strains >40%.
The Al-, C-containing alloy exhibited dislocation densities approximately two times higher than the reference CoCrFeNiMn alloy at comparable strains.
item.mechanism: The addition of Al and C increases the stacking fault energy (SFE), which suppresses early twinning and promotes planar dislocation slip; this results in higher dislocation density accumulation and a delayed onset of deformation twinning, shifting the dominant strengthening mechanism from substructure hardening at low strains to Hall-Petch (twin boundary) strengthening at high strains.
item.limitations: The text notes that exact calculation of the SFE value is a complex problem and could not be fully evaluated due to the absence of other input values for the adapted equation, though the relative difference was confirmed via ∆Ghcp−fcc calculations.
item.future_work: The authors state that additional studies on the effects of alloying on deformation mechanisms of CoCrFeNiMn-type alloys are required, noting that the effect of Al is even less studied than carbon.
quotes: The alloy with a chemical composition (at %) of (20–23) Co, Cr, Fe, and Ni; 8.82 Mn; 3.37 Al; and 0.69 C was produced by self-propagating high-temperature synthesis with subsequent induction.

A comparison with the equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn alloy revealed higher dislocation density at all stages of cold rolling and later onset of deformation twinning that was attributed to a stacking fault energy increase in the program alloy.
Substructure strengthening was found to be dominated at low rolling reductions (<40%), while grain (twin) boundary strengthening prevailed at higher strains.
